- **When:** Wednesdays, 10:00–12:00 and 13:30–15:30 (two sessions per day, same content each session – attendees can choose morning or afternoon)
- **Where:** Makerspace Room, ground floor, near the children's area
- **Max capacity per session:** 12 participants (including carers/parents if they stay to assist)
- **Age range:** 10 years and up; under 14s must be accompanied by an adult
- **Cost:** Free, but registration is required (book online or at the front desk; we usually fill up within 2–3 days of opening bookings)

**Staff allocation**

Each session is staffed by **two facilitators** for a total of **4 hours per session** (one facilitator leads the main activity, the other floats to help individuals and manage the queue for the 3D printer). This allocation has been in place since the start of the summer schedule and remains current for the whole period.

- **Lead facilitator:** rotates weekly between Tom and Priya (see roster below)
- **Floating facilitator:** drawn from the casual pool – usually one of Hannah, Marcus, or Jess

**Weekly roster (1 Dec – 28 Feb)**

Makerspace Workshop has a staff_hours_per_session of 4 hours per session according to the program schedule. Record status: current.

**Materials and consumables (per session)**

- **3D printing:** 1 kg PLA filament per session (shared between the two sessions; we have 8 spools in stock as of 28 Nov – please reorder when we're down to 3)
- **Sewing:** fabric is donated/from offcuts; thread, needles, and pins are in the red toolbox. Check the bobbin case before each session – we ran out mid-session last term and it caused a 20-minute delay.
- **Cricut/vinyl:** vinyl sheets (A4) – 12 per session; transfer tape – we need to restock, currently down to 2 rolls. Order placed 25 Nov with Officeworks, ETA 9 Dec.
- **General:** rubbing alcohol and paper towel for cleaning the machines after each session; hand sanitiser at the door; disposable gloves for glue gun use (we have a box under the sink).

**Safety protocols (unchanged this quarter)**

- All machines must be switched off and unplugged at the end of the final session each day. Tom is the named person responsible for the last Wednesday of each month; otherwise the floating facilitator does it.
- 3D printer: no loose hair or sleeves near the print bed; heated bed is 60°C – we put a laminated warning sign next to the machine.
- Sewing machines: needle guard must stay in place. We had a minor incident in October where a child put their finger near the needle – no injury, but we reviewed the rule with all staff and now do a 2-minute safety talk at the start of every sewing session.
- Glue guns: only used by adults or by children with an adult's hand on the gun. We keep the glue guns in a locked cupboard when not in use.
- If a participant has an allergy or sensitivity to any material (e.g., latex gloves, certain fabrics), they should let us know at registration and we'll adjust.

**Special projects (notable items this quarter)**

- **Print4Good initiative:** In partnership with the local primary school, we're 3D printing replacement parts for their sensory toys (the school has a set of fidget spinners and puzzle cubes that have broken over the years). We're doing this as a "print while you wait" add-on – participants can watch their design print while we run the school's parts in the background. The school liaison is Sarah from the front office; she'll drop off the broken parts on 6 Jan and we'll aim to have everything printed by the end of February. This doesn't change the staff allocation – the floating facilitator monitors the background prints.

This is an extra event, not part of the regular Wednesday sessions, and will be staffed separately – Tom and Priya are both confirmed, plus two volunteers from the Friends of the Library group. Volunteer coordination is with Hannah; she'll send a reminder email in early February.
- **Sewing repair café (one-off):** On Saturday 7 Feb, we're running a repair café where people can bring in clothes and household items for mending. This is a separate booking from the regular program – Priya is leading, and we're borrowing two extra machines from the community centre. The centre's machines are older and may need a service; Marcus will check them on 4 Feb.
